podcast.title: Collaboration with Colonel Tom Parker
podcast.body: Mae Axton frequently worked with Colonel Tom Parker to promote shows when they came through Florida, where she resided. "she would often work with Colonel Parker on promoting shows when they came through Flavida, where she lived."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Inspired by Elvis's Family Devotion
podcast.body: After interviewing Elvis in Florida, Mae Axton was deeply struck by his earnest desire to earn enough money to bring his parents to live there, inspiring her to promise to write him a song. "She said later, that just went through my heart, because I looked down there, and there were all these other kids, different show members for that night, all the guys looking for cute little girls. But his priority was doing something for his mother and daddy."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Publicist for Hank Snow
podcast.body: For a period, Mae Axton served as the personal publicist for country singer Hank Snow. "For a time, she was Hank Snow's personal publicist."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Unexpected Songwriting Debut
podcast.body: An English teacher and freelance journalist, Mae Axton initially knew nothing about "Hilboly music." Her songwriting career began unexpectedly when Mini Pearl falsely introduced her as a songwriter to Fred Rose of Acuff-Rose Publishing, leading to her being asked to write a novelty song for Dub Dickerson. "And so all of a sudden, May Axton was a songwriter, and she eventually wrote over 200 songs."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
